Documentation / Developer / Document typography and font licensing

Document typography and font licensing

Perastage resolves the requested family, weight and style to the exact approved font bytes before composition. FontCatalog owns immutable resource data, version, PostScript face name, OFL provenance and SHA-256. Rendering targets use the resolved fingerprint and glyph ID. Persisted styles keep the family and variant authored by the user, so substituting a face does not change the project.

Approved resources

PerastageSans is the application name for the original Noto Sans face. It is the default family. The Noto Sans and Noto Serif files come from Debian fonts-noto-core 20201225-2. Source Sans 3 comes from Adobe's 3.052R release. Third-party notices identify the exact releases, files and licenses. Only those SHA-256 identities enter the first catalog. The files are static single-face TrueType fonts with unrestricted embedding flags. An unrestricted OS/2.fsType on its own gives no license evidence.

The catalog checks packaged resources during application initialization. When an approved file is missing or unusable, the system adapter searches the usual font directories for that platform. It filters candidates by size before validating format, embedding flags and SHA-256 and accepts byte-identical matches under any filename. Bundled resources are preferred. The search covers Windows Fonts and the per-user Microsoft Fonts directory, macOS system, local and user Fonts directories, and Linux standard, XDG and user font directories. Custom platform font registration paths outside these directories are outside this discovery scope. Arbitrary installed family names and user-supplied paths do not authorize use. Perastage does not install fonts or attach them to projects.

CFF, collections, web fonts and variable fonts are unsupported. Additions need a verified provenance and rights record, pinned bytes, a supported outline and cmap check, exact installed-package files and the upstream license text. The application uses the same package contract on Windows, Linux and macOS.

Composition and adapters

The existing TrueType reader supplies glyph advances and vertical metrics. The text compositor works in scene metres or document points. It decodes UTF-8 through the font's Unicode cmap (formats 4 and 12). The glyph plan records the original character, resolved face, glyph ID, advance, position and baseline. A missing glyph uses the approved default of the same variant where available. Unavailable characters use the face's missing-character contour and retain the original source. Western European text including precomposed Spanish accents, common punctuation, Greek and Cyrillic are supported where covered by the face. Combining-mark positioning, bidirectional text, OpenType shaping and contextual ligatures require a shaping library. FreeType would provide outline extraction and rasterization but would not supply this shaping. HarfBuzz and bidi processing were deferred to avoid introducing dependencies for an unqualified repertoire. The common compositor reports missing or unsupported glyphs.

Fixture Label Editor drafts, source 2D labels and Layout capture share their existing field composition. The default face preserves the established NanoVG halo and the shared positions. Other approved faces use their glyph contours. Layout replay renders the captured contours with the stored physical outline widths. Raster antialiasing and the zoom-independent 2D halo policy may differ from paper ink.

Free text uses the same point-space text block plan for Layout and PDF. Rich text remains serialized in its original wx XML model. Extraction preserves families, weights, sizes, italic requests, foreground colors, underlines, strikethrough, explicit breaks, paragraph alignment, spacing and indentation. Approved family selections enable word wrapping. Existing text without an explicit approved family retains explicit line breaks and clipping. Legacy native-font metrics could vary by platform. Default sizing now uses the shipped faces, so historical free-text widths can change. Non-text rich objects and uncommon XML style features remain in the source XML with limited rendering support. Noto Sans Italic and Bold Italic preserve italic styling using real faces. Requests for italic in the other two families fall back to the corresponding Noto Sans italic face. A wx rich-text control is used for editing and can display a native fallback on builds without private font registration. The Layout canvas supplies the document rendering.

Legend and Event Table retain their shared point-space composition and size formulas from the integration branch. The older split-export PDF compensation had already been replaced there. Fixture names retain their historical two-space-delimited-word breaks. Viewport capture and Layout raster archives invalidate incompatible plans. The existing per-viewport label cache and bounded shared outline cache avoid repeating glyph work.

PDF output and persistence

The exporter uses Type 0 fonts with TrueType CIDFont descendants, an explicit CID-to-glyph map and a ToUnicode CMap. CIDs encode both the selected glyph and original codepoint, including surrogate pairs when required. The PDF places glyphs at the composed positions. It draws fixture outlines as vector paths and leaves the glyph fill selectable. Only used approved faces are embedded. Missing faces and unsupported glyphs are recorded once per issue in the export report. Font resource failure leaves scene contents and requested style values intact.

Label presentation version 3 adds the optional fontFamily field. Layout's presentation wrapper reads both versions 2 and 3. Unchanged label styles continue to write version 2. Legends and Event Tables have an optional fontFamily property in the existing Layout schema and use the default when the field is absent. Free text retains its existing per-run rich-text data. PSTG and templates store presentation choices without introducing font data into MVR or GDTF. Reopening a project revalidates an incomplete catalog, allowing restored packaged or installed resources to recover the requested appearance.

Verification

PdfFontMetricsEncoding covers catalog authorization, exact installed-face recovery, actual glyph identity, fallback, advances and mixed-family runs. LayoutLicensedFontsPdf uses Poppler to validate a representative Layout's faces, Unicode extraction, and outline/selection behavior. Layout preview and PDF tests compare geometry in document points. The raster parity tests compare ink geometry with tolerances for antialiasing and rasterizer differences.
